groups.name: Bulk RNA-seq raw count matrix
groups.description: A single CSV of raw (integer-valued, unnormalized) RNA-seq counts: 5702 genes (rows) by 12 samples (sample_01..sample_12, columns), gene symbols as row identifiers. This is the primary measurement table for differential expression analysis.
groups.memberRepresents: The gene x sample raw read-count matrix for the entire experiment (one row per gene, one column per sample)

groups.name: Sample sheet
groups.description: A 12-row sample sheet with columns `sample` (sample_01..sample_12, matching the count matrix's column names exactly) and `condition` (control/treated, 6 vs 6). This is the design table that defines the two-group comparison.
groups.memberRepresents: The full sample-to-condition mapping for the experiment (one row per sample)

groups.name: Gene length reference table
groups.description: A two-column lookup table (gene, length) for 12000 genes, a superset of the genes in the count matrix. Consumed, not produced, by this analysis — used to convert raw counts to length-normalized units (e.g. TPM/FPKM) if needed downstream.
groups.categoryReason: A static gene-id-to-length lookup table the analysis consumes for normalization; it is not itself a measurement, so reference-data (role reference) fits better than sample-annotation or expression-matrix.
groups.memberRepresents: The transcript/gene length in bp for one gene, used for length-normalization

probes.reason: metadata.csv has only `sample` and `condition` columns; each sample_XX appears to be an independent biological replicate with no subject-level identifier or repeated-measures structure.
No date, visit, day, or cycle column in metadata.csv; only sample id and condition.
No plate, lane, run, or centre column in metadata.csv; only sample id and condition.

caveats: Organism is not stated anywhere in the inputs; identification as human rests solely on HGNC-style all-caps gene symbol casing, a weak indirect signal — confirm before selecting species-specific annotation/pathway references.

Normalization state of counts.csv is raw, unnormalized integer read counts (values include small integers alongside larger ones, no evidence of library-size or length scaling) — appropriate for count-based DE tools (e.g. DESeq2/edgeR) but not for direct cross-sample comparison without normalization.
No batch, timepoint, pairing, or subject-level metadata exists beyond sample id and condition — the design supports only a simple two-group comparison, not blocking or repeated-measures models.

gene_lengths.csv covers 12000 genes versus roughly 5702 genes in counts.csv; the two were not cross-checked for full gene-id overlap here, so a downstream step doing length-normalization should verify how many count-matrix genes actually have a matching length entry.

Gene set size (~5702 genes) is small relative to a typical whole-transcriptome bulk RNA-seq matrix (~15,000-20,000+ detected genes), consistent with this being a reduced/smoke-test dataset rather than a full production count matrix.
result.summary: The dataset is a minimal bulk RNA-seq experiment ready for a two-group differential expression analysis: a raw gene x sample count matrix (5702 genes x 12 samples), a matching 12-row sample sheet assigning each sample to 'control' (n=6) or 'treated' (n=6), and a gene-length reference table (12000 genes) for length-normalization. There are no documents, READMEs, or accessions in the input tree to corroborate organism, tissue, or study context — all three files are local CSVs with no accompanying metadata beyond the sample sheet itself. Organism is inferred only weakly (from gene symbol casing) as Homo sapiens; tissue and cell type are not stated and are left null. The design is a clean, balanced two-arm case/control comparison with no batch, timepoint, or pairing structure evidenced, and the small gene count suggests this is a reduced or smoke-test dataset rather than a full-scale transcriptome-wide study — appropriate for exercising a DE + downstream enrichment pipeline end-to-end, but not for drawing biological conclusions about a real tissue/condition without further context.

organism.notes: No explicit organism label anywhere in the inputs (no README/metadata organism column). Gene symbols (ABCA1, ABCB8, ACAA2, ACADL, ...) are in the all-caps HGNC convention typically used for human, as opposed to the Title-case MGI convention used for mouse. This is only a weak, indirect signal — orthologous genes share symbols across species — so confidence is low and this should be verified before choosing a species-specific reference/annotation.

dimensions.label: condition (control vs treated)
dimensions.description: Design-assigned two-arm grouping: 6 samples labeled 'control', 6 labeled 'treated' in metadata.csv. This is the primary comparison axis for differential expression.

result.experimentalDesign: Simple two-group case/control bulk RNA-seq design: 12 samples total, balanced 6 control vs 6 treated, one sample per condition-replicate (no stated pairing, batch, or timepoint structure). Sized and shaped like a minimal/smoke-test dataset (5702 genes) rather than a full transcriptome-wide production dataset, suitable for a straightforward two-group differential expression comparison (e.g. control vs treated) followed by downstream enrichment analysis.
